_note: The channel table make_confs.py turns into rtl_airband configs. This is the ONE file whose contents depend on where you are. Sets marked "replace_me": true are refused by make_confs.py until you edit them -- a placeholder frequency does not fail loudly, it records silence and looks healthy doing it, so the generator will not let you run one by accident.
_how_to_find_your_own: Run the survey lanes first and read the output before recording anything:
air_survey sweeps 118-137 MHz and shows which airband channels near you are actually live.
milair_survey sweeps 225-400 MHz for military air.
Public references (RadioReference, your national regulator's licence database) tell you what SHOULD be there; the survey tells you what IS. Trust the survey.

A peak-hold sweep OVERSTATES a burst: +16 dB on a 30 s peak-hold is not a +16 dB transmission, and on this author's site six channels that looked busy produced zero audio in 317 runs. Confirm with a recorded lane before believing a frequency.

guard121.note: International aviation DISTRESS. Expected silent; a recording here matters. Same frequency worldwide.

guard243.note: Military UHF guard/distress -- the 121.5 twin. Same frequency worldwide.

frs.note: All 15 FRS/GMRS 462 channels -- 175 kHz block, one slice, simultaneous. US allocation. 'Privacy codes' are CTCSS squelch tones, NOT encryption.

frs467.note: FRS 8-14 low-power block at 467. US allocation.

murs.note: MURS 1-3 (151 block). US allocation. MURS 4-5 at 154.57/154.60 are 2.7 MHz away and need their own slice.

vhf_fire.note: US VHF fire mutual-aid (VFIRE21-23). Nationally allocated, but whether anything near you still simulcasts in the clear is local and increasingly rare -- most agencies have moved to 700/800 MHz. Confirm with a sweep before enabling the lane.

air_tower.note: REPLACE: your local tower and approach. Channels within about 1.5 MHz of each other land in one 2.4 MHz slice and are heard simultaneously; further apart needs a second set. Find them with the air_survey lane, or from your national aeronautical publication.

air_ground.note: REPLACE: your local ground control. ATIS is usually 2+ MHz away -- past the usable passband -- and is a repeating loop with little to say, so it is normally not worth a slice.

milair.note: REPLACE: UHF military air near you. These three are spacing placeholders, not real assignments -- seed them from milair_survey output. The lane stays disabled in lanes.json until you do.
